title: The Orphanage
subtitle: /El orfanato
review: In haunting stories like this, the person being haunted is always so convinced that what they've experienced is real. Here, the mother is sure that she is seeing real paranormal activity, and ignores the professionals who say it's all in her head. But misplacing a child would obviously be so stressful it could easily cause delusions like that. We are convinced that dreams are real, as they're happening, and there are several known conditions that cause false experiences or memories, so why are we surprised that we might see things that aren't real? If it happened to me I would assume I was suffering from a mental health issue, before any idea of the supernatural ever crossed my mind. I am sometimes convinced that I just heard my doorbell ring, and that I was awake and alert for it, when in reality it's a auditory hallucination just as I wake up. It seems so convincingly real when it happens, although it took about a year in my new house for this phenomenon to switch to my new doorbell sound. If I lost a son, and started seeing a little boy the same size and shape out of the corner of my eye on dark nights, why wouldn't I listen to the experts with a rational explanation? Anyway that's not the case here, and it wouldn't be a horror movie if it was. There are definitely real ghosts and the mother is not driven insane by grief. It's a great movie but it's a little derivative of other sad haunted house tales.
